subject: Re: Frontloaded credit structure & GPU rollout schedule
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@helios.ai>; Kevin Long <kevin.long@helios.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Frontloaded credit structure & GPU rollout schedule

Alice / Kevin —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our conversation, I attached a short capacity plan and two commercial options that try to balance Helios's desire to frontload availability with Redwood's need for predictable committed revenue. High level:

- Proposal A (smoother): 2-year annual prepay with a staggered GPU/TPM ramp over 12 months (25% / 25% / 25% / 25%). 12% term discount on list pricing across the committed units.
- Proposal B (frontloaded accelerator): 2-year annual prepay but with a frontloaded delivery (50% available in month 1, remainder ramped over next 6 months). 10% base term discount plus a one-time accelerator credit applied to usage in the first 9 months (credit amount and cap negotiable).

Ask from our side: if you can commit to an accelerated delivery (Proposal B) we can shift additional unit economics (accelerator credit + shorter credit amortization) to reduce your effective $/TPM in the first year. We kept the accelerator as a credit (applied against monthly invoices) rather than an up-front rebate to keep bookkeeping simple for procurement.

Attachments: 2026-08-capacity-plan.xlsx (capacity milestones, month-by-month GPU & TPM availability), redwood-tos-v3.pdf (commercial terms, SOW language for staggered delivery).

Could you confirm which model you prefer and whether your procurement/legal team will accept credits applied against invoices? If you prefer, we can propose a strict milestone schedule with breakpoints that trigger additional discount steps.

Next steps: happy to jump on a 30-minute call w/ procurement this week.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Sean —

Thanks for the clear options and the attachments. A few quick items from procurement and engineering:

- We like Proposal B (frontload) from a product launch perspective. Getting more capacity earlier materially shortens our time-to-revenue.
- Procurement wants a clear definition of the breakpoints that move us between discount tiers (e.g., % committed by month X). We also need the credits to be documented in the contract appendix (not just invoicing notes).
- Legal prefers an accelerator structured as a capped credit applied monthly rather than a lump-sum rebate — that should be fine. Please state the cap and the amortization window.
- Security asked whether any special attestations are required for the accelerated capacity (short answer: no, standard SOC2 + VPC private deployment will cover it).

Could you put a concrete numeric proposal in writing (credit amount, cap, milestone dates) so we can share with procurement/legal? Also please confirm the cancellation / scaling down rights after month 12.

Appreciate it —

Date: 2026-09-02T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Helios - frontload request (need approval on concessions)

Laura / Marissa —

Looping you in on Helios's ask (quoted below). They like the frontloaded option and asked for concrete numbers: credit amount, cap, and milestone dates. They want the credit captured in the contract appendix and prefer monthly-applied capped credits.

My proposal for approval before I send a counter:
- Commercial structure: 2-year annual prepay (Year 1 and Year 2 invoices up front).
- Term discount: base 12% off list on committed units.
- Accelerator: $150,000 in accelerator credits applied across months 1–9 (applied to monthly invoices). Cap at $200,000 total (i.e., we offer $150k but will accept up to $200k as a negotiable cap).
- Milestones / breakpoints: If Helios funds >=70% of Year 1 committed units within 90 days, increase term discount to 15% for Year 1 (retroactive credit applied in month 4 invoice). If they hit 90% by 60 days, we can consider a 18% year-1 discount (exec approval required).
- Overages: standard pay-as-you-go at list rate; if usage exceeds committed runway, we discount overage pricing by 5% for the remainder of Year 1.
- Cancellation / scale-down: they can reduce future year commitments with 120 days' notice but for Year 1 prepay is non-refundable (standard amortization language applies).

Rationale: accelerator credits reduce Helios's near-term cash OPEX hit while preserving our committed revenue recognition. The breakpoint approach gives Helios runway flexibility while protecting Redwood economics.

Can we push back on the retroactive increase to discount (15% retroactive) without exec sign-off? My preference: approve 12% base + $150k accelerator with a 15% contingent discount triggered prospectively (not retroactively). If they want retroactive, require exec sign-off.

Thanks —Sean

Laura Bennett replied: "I can approve 12% base + $150k accelerator. 15% contingent is fine if legal signs a delivery addendum; retroactive credit requires CRO ok."

Marissa Cole replied: "Recommend we cap accelerator at $200k absolute and limit retroactive adjustments to 30 days back. Also suggest we formalize amortization schedule in appendix."

Alice / Kevin —

Thanks for the quick follow-up. Based on internal approvals, here is a concrete offer you can review with procurement/legal this week:

1) Commercial skeleton (2-year annual prepay)
- Year 1 & Year 2 prepaid at contract signature.
- Base term discount: 12% on committed units (applies both years).

2) Accelerator credit (frontload economics)
- Redwood will provide $150,000 in accelerator credits applied monthly across months 1–9.
- Credit cap: $200,000 (we will not exceed this).
- Credits applied against monthly invoices; documented in contract appendix as a credit schedule.

3) Breakpoint incentive (conditional additional discount)
- If Helios funds >= 70% of Year 1 committed units within 90 days of signature, Redwood will increase Year 1 term discount to 15%.
- If Helios funds >= 90% within 60 days, Redwood will consider an 18% Year 1 discount (this requires final sign-off from CRO and Legal; we will document as an executive escalation lane).

4) Overages & scaling
- Overages billed at list rate with a 5% overage discount for the remainder of Year 1 if usage exceeds the committed runway.
- Year 2 scaling down allowed with 120 days notice; Year 1 annual prepay remains non-refundable (standard amortization and SOW appendix will reflect milestones).

5) Contract mechanics
- Accelerator credits will be spelled out in the contract appendix (credit table + amortization months).
- Any retroactive application of additional discount beyond 30 days will require executive sign-off; we will document the retroactive window in the appendix.

Attachments: updated capacity plan (2026-08-capacity-plan.xlsx) and the current commercial terms (redwood-tos-v3.pdf). I can share a one-page addendum with the credit table for procurement/legal if helpful.

If this looks acceptable, can we schedule a 30-minute procurement call on Friday 9/4 to get signatures moving? If you prefer alternate timings, I can accommodate next week as well.

Regards,
